evidence.quote:
There is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for every pair of complex functions $F,G\in L^3(\mathbb R^2)$, $$\|B_*(F,G)\|_{L^{3/2}(\mathbb R^2)}
 \le C\|F\|_{L^3(\mathbb R^2)}\|G\|_{L^3(\mathbb R^2)}.$$ The supremum is over both finite hard truncation endpoints.

exclusions.query: Uniform estimates at arbitrary input exponents
exclusions.reason: The main assertion fixes the input and output Lebesgue spaces.

evidence.quote: The pointwise maximal optimal constant is at least $C_S$.

exclusions.query: Equality of scalar and pointwise maximal optimal constants
exclusions.reason: The paper gives a lower bound for the maximal optimal constant, rather than equality.

outputs.exact_statement:
There is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for every pair of complex functions $F,G\in L^3(\mathbb R^2)$, $$\|B_*(F,G)\|_{L^{3/2}(\mathbb R^2)}
 \le C\|F\|_{L^3(\mathbb R^2)}\|G\|_{L^3(\mathbb R^2)}.$$ The supremum is over both finite hard truncation endpoints.

Let $P,Q$ be positive semidefinite matrices on the same Hilbert space, let $a\ge1$, and suppose $P\le aQ$. Every Hermitian $K$ supported on $P$ is supported on $Q$, and $$\label{eq:matrix-order}
 b_P(K)\ge a^{-1/2}b_Q(K).$$

Let $W_v:H_{v+1}\to H_v$ be linear maps between finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, with row stars $R_v$ and Gram matrices $T_v$ as in [eq:row-star]–[eq:star-grams]. For Hermitian maps $D_v:H_v\to H_v$, put $D_* =\max_v\lVert D_v\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}$. Then $$\label{eq:mixed-trace} \left|\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}(D_0W_0D_1W_1D_2W_2)\right| \le \frac53D_*\sum_{v=0}^2 b_{T_v}(R_v^*D_vR_v).$$ The constant is independent of the dimensions of the spaces.

For fixed finite edge arrays, each $e_v$ is smooth in all centers and positive variances. If only the parameters at vertex $v$ vary, the support of $T_v$ is fixed. If the parameters at either or both other vertices vary while those at $v$ are fixed, the support of $S_v$ is fixed.

Fix a positive vector $\boldsymbol\alpha$ and set $\sigma_i=\alpha_i s$. For all centers and all $s>0$, $$\begin{aligned}
 2\partial_s e_v
 &=\sum_i\alpha_i\partial_{p_i}^2e_v
       -\alpha_vV_v-\sum_{w\ne v}\alpha_wY_{v,w},
       \label{eq:heat-identity}\\
 \partial_{p_{v+1}}\partial_{p_{v-1}}e_v&=Z_v.
       \label{eq:heat-mixed}
\end{aligned}$$

For every choice of the weighted matrices and every vertex $w$, $$\label{eq:heat-neighbors}
 Y_{w+1,w}+Y_{w-1,w}\le\sqrt2\,V_w.$$

Fix finite edge arrays and a positive vector $\boldsymbol\alpha$, and evaluate the energies at $\sigma_i=\alpha_i s$. Set $$J_v(d,s)=\int_{\Pi_d}e_v\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\pi_d,
 \qquad J(d,s)=\sum_vJ_v(d,s),
 \qquad \Sigma_\alpha=\sum_i\alpha_i.$$ These integrals are finite, continuously differentiable in $s>0$, and twice continuously differentiable in $d$. Moreover, $$\label{eq:heat-plane-dissipation}
 2\partial_sJ(d,s)\le\int_{\Pi_d}\sum_w
 \left[-\alpha_w+
 \sqrt2\max\{0,\Sigma_\alpha/2-\alpha_w\}\right]V_w\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\pi_d.$$ In particular, for each permutation of $(1,\lambda,\lambda)$, $$\label{eq:heat-strict}
 -\partial_sJ(d,s)\ge c_*\int_{\Pi_d}\sum_wV_w\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\pi_d,
 \qquad
 c_* = \frac12\min\{1-\tfrac35\sqrt2,\tfrac{11}{10}-\tfrac12\sqrt2\}>0.$$

Let $h>0$, let $N\ge0$ be an integer, and let $A_v(i,j)$ be the finite complex arrays above. For any $d\in\mathbb R$ and variances $\sigma_v\ge h^2$, $$\label{eq:initial-energy}
 \int_{\Pi_d}\sum_ve_v\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\pi_d
 \le C_0\mathcal S(A),\qquad
 C_0=2\sqrt2\left(1+\sqrt{2/\pi}\right).$$ The same bound holds if any entries are replaced by smaller entries in absolute value before forming the weighted matrices.

Let $h>0$, let $N\ge0$ be an integer, set $u_i=ih$, and let $A_v(i,j)$, $v=0,1,2$, be complex arrays indexed by $-N\le i,j\le N$. Assign an arbitrary endpoint pair $h\le\varepsilon_{ij}<\rho_{ij}<\infty$ to each $(i,j)$. Then $$\label{eq:selected-kernel}
 \left|h^3\sum_{i,j,l}A_0(i,j)A_1(j,l)A_2(l,i)
       I_{\varepsilon_{ij},\rho_{ij}}(u_i+u_j+u_l)\right|
 \le C\prod_{v=0}^2\left(\sum_{i,j}h^2|A_v(i,j)|^3\right)^{1/3}.$$ The constant is independent of the arrays, mesh and selected endpoints.

For complex $F,G\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ and every $r>0$, $$\left|\int_\mathbb RF(x+t,y)G(x,y+t)E_r(t)\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dt\right|
 \le C\bigl[M_x(|F|^2)(x,y)M_y(|G|^2)(x,y)\bigr]^{1/2}.$$ The right side has $L^{3/2}(\mathbb R^2)$ norm at most $C\|F\|_3\|G\|_3$.

For all complex $F,G\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$, $$\|B_*(F,G)\|_{L^{3/2}(\mathbb R^2)}
 \le C\|F\|_{L^3(\mathbb R^2)}\|G\|_{L^3(\mathbb R^2)},$$ with an absolute constant. The supremum defining $B_*$ is over both finite hard truncation endpoints, inside the spatial norm.
